paragraphs: Generating convincing views of an object does not necessarily mean recovering its correct three-dimensional shape. The paper addresses ambiguity between shape and color: different combinations can produce realistic images, even when the underlying geometry is inaccurate.

The proposed model adds a lighting requirement to the usual requirement that objects look realistic from multiple viewpoints. It explicitly represents illumination and renders objects under different lighting conditions. A discriminator evaluates the generated images, supplying gradients that guide learning toward shapes whose shading also looks plausible.

Computing surface normals for shading adds work. To offset that cost, the authors introduce a volume-rendering strategy based on tracking the surface. They report reductions of 24% in training time and 48% in inference time.

Experiments across multiple datasets show photorealistic image generation alongside improved underlying shapes. The paper also reports better shape reconstruction than existing methods and demonstrates image relighting. Its central contribution is using appearance under changing illumination as an additional source of guidance for learning geometry.
neurips-2021-a-shading-guided-generative.tldr: Explicitly modeling lighting helps a generative image model learn more accurate 3D shapes while supporting realistic rendering and relighting.

paragraphs: Vision transformers can perform well on visual tasks, but their computational demands complicate deployment on mobile devices. This paper investigates reducing their energy consumption through AdderNet, bringing addition-based computation into the attention mechanism.

The authors first examine why simply applying adder operations to self-attention is difficult. Their analysis identifies a problem with preserving feature diversity, expressed through the rank of the attention map. An attention mechanism that loses this diversity may have a reduced ability to represent different aspects of an image.

To address that problem, they introduce an adder attention layer with an additional identity mapping. This modification is intended to preserve useful representations while allowing the transformer to rely on additions. The architectural change follows directly from the difficulty identified in their theoretical analysis.

Across several benchmarks, the resulting models achieve performance that is highly competitive with the baselines while reducing energy consumption by approximately a factor of two to three. These findings support the approach as a way to improve energy efficiency without a large reported loss in predictive performance.
neurips-2021-adder-attention-for-vision-.tldr: Adder attention adds an identity mapping to preserve useful features while delivering competitive vision performance with roughly two to three times lower energy consumption.

paragraphs: Feature selection reduces the number of inputs a learning system uses by retaining an informative subset. This can make the resulting analysis easier to interpret. The paper focuses on unsupervised selection and on whether selected features remain stable when the input samples change.

The proposed algorithm combines two linked components. A neural network scores all features globally, while a dependent subnetwork evaluates their ability to represent the data locally. Together, these components connect broad feature scoring with the more focused task of choosing a subset.

The authors analyze algorithmic stability, meaning sensitivity to changes in the sample used by the algorithm. They establish stability guarantees and a generalization error bound. This connects the selection procedure to a theoretical performance guarantee beyond its behavior on the observed samples.

Experiments on real-world datasets show better generalization than strong baseline methods. They also empirically support properties identified by the theory and the stability of the selected features. The contribution therefore combines a selection architecture with evidence about both its predictive usefulness and its consistency under sample perturbations.
neurips-2021-algorithmic-stability-and-g.tldr: A paired neural scorer and selector provides unsupervised feature selection with stability guarantees and strong empirical generalization.

paragraphs: Energy-based models offer a framework for estimating probability densities, but training them is difficult. This paper builds on a connection to generative adversarial networks, where learning is organized as a minimax game using a variational objective.

The authors introduce bounds on the model's log-likelihood from both directions. Their training procedure maximizes a lower bound while minimizing an upper bound. This gives the opposing parts of the game a shared statistical target, approached through quantities that constrain it from below and above.

One of these bounds is connected to a gradient penalty used to stabilize training. That connection gives a theoretical basis for an existing engineering practice. The paper also develops an efficient estimator of the generator's Jacobian determinant so that the proposed bounds can be evaluated.

The reported demonstrations show more stable training together with high-quality density estimates and generated samples. The contribution links a statistical training objective, a practical stabilization mechanism, and a computational tool needed to evaluate the objective within one approach.
neurips-2021-bounds-all-around-training-.tldr: Training energy-based models with upper and lower likelihood bounds provides a principled route to more stable learning and high-quality generation.

paragraphs: Large vision transformers are costly to train and run, and pruning after training can require additional training expenditure. This paper investigates incorporating sparsity throughout learning to reduce training memory and inference computation while preserving achievable accuracy.

The method dynamically extracts and trains sparse subnetworks under a fixed, small parameter budget. It updates both the numerical parameters and the network's connectivity, producing a single sparse network at the end. The approach also supports structured sparsity by pruning and growing self-attention heads.

A learnable token selector extends the efficiency effort to the input data. It adaptively selects the image patches currently judged most important, allowing the method to explore data sparsity and architectural sparsity together.

ImageNet experiments with several transformer backbones report substantially lower computational cost and nearly unchanged generalization, with accuracy sometimes improving. One DeiT-Small configuration reports a 0.28% top-1 accuracy improvement, 49.32% fewer FLOPs, and 4.40% running-time savings. Those separate savings show that reduced operation counts and actual speed improvements are distinct reported outcomes.
neurips-2021-chasing-sparsity-in-vision-.tldr: Dynamically training sparse vision transformers and selecting useful image patches reduces computation while largely preserving, and sometimes improving, accuracy.

paragraphs: Generating images from unrestricted text requires both an image-generation capability and an understanding of how language relates to visual content. CogView addresses this combination with a four-billion-parameter Transformer and a VQ-VAE tokenizer.

The tokenizer supplies a token-based representation for images, allowing the proposed system to bring image generation into a Transformer framework. The paper presents this large model as an approach to the broad text-to-image problem, where the requested content is not restricted to a narrow domain.

The work also addresses making the model usable beyond its initial training objective. It demonstrates fine-tuning strategies for learning styles, increasing image resolution, ranking text-image pairs, and fashion design. Methods for stabilizing pretraining, including eliminating NaN losses, address practical difficulties in training the system.

CogView achieves the reported best FID on the blurred MS COCO dataset, outperforming previous GAN-based models and DALL-E in that evaluation. This is evidence for its generation quality on the stated benchmark, while the fine-tuning demonstrations show the range of downstream tasks explored with the model.
neurips-2021-cogview-mastering-text-to-i.tldr: CogView combines a large Transformer with image tokenization, stable pretraining, and task-specific fine-tuning to advance text-to-image generation.

paragraphs: Standard backpropagation updates a neuron's weights using information about downstream weights. This nonlocal dependence makes it difficult to interpret as a biological learning mechanism. Feedback alignment instead uses fixed random weights to carry information backward.

The paper studies the mathematics of feedback alignment in two-layer networks trained with squared error loss. It separates two questions: whether the prediction error approaches zero, and whether learned parameters become aligned with the random feedback weights.

In the overparameterized setting considered, the authors prove that the error decreases to zero exponentially fast. They also show that regularization is necessary for parameter alignment in their analysis. These results distinguish successful error reduction from the separate property of alignment with the feedback pathway.

Simulations agree with the analysis and suggest possible generalizations. The findings contribute to understanding how a more biologically plausible learning procedure could achieve performance comparable to full backpropagation. The formal conclusions concern the stated network, loss, and overparameterized setting; the suggested extensions go beyond what those proofs establish.
neurips-2021-convergence-and-alignment-o.tldr: For overparameterized two-layer networks, feedback alignment achieves exponentially vanishing error, while parameter alignment requires regularization in the analyzed setting.

paragraphs: Probabilistic Watershed assigns labels on a graph using a small set of labeled nodes called seeds. Its original form works with undirected graphs and assigns probabilities according to how nodes connect to seeds across possible spanning forests.

This paper extends the construction to directed graphs, where edge direction matters. The method places a Gibbs probability distribution over incoming directed forests rooted at the seeds. Using the directed Matrix Tree Theorem, it builds a probabilistic labeling procedure that respects those directed connections.

The authors show that this construction is equivalent to the Directed Random Walker. They also characterize a limiting case: as the Gibbs temperature approaches zero, its labeling matches that induced by the minimum-cost incoming directed forest. This links the probabilistic formulation to a cost-minimizing forest construction.

The paper illustrates the method through empirical comparisons with other semi-supervised segmentation approaches for directed graphs. Its stated theoretical contribution is the connection among directed forest probabilities, random walks, and minimum-cost labeling, providing several complementary views of the same labeling problem.
neurips-2021-directed-probabilistic-wate.tldr: Directed Probabilistic Watershed extends seed-based graph labeling to directed edges and connects it to random walks and minimum-cost forests.

paragraphs: Adversarial robustness evaluation asks how small an input change can make a model misclassify a sample. Finding such changes is an optimization problem, and existing gradient-based attacks can demand careful tuning, special starting points, or many expensive iterations.

The proposed fast minimum-norm attack, FMN, adapts the permitted perturbation size during optimization. Within the current constraint, it searches for a sample that is misclassified with high confidence. It then adjusts the constraint to reduce the sample's distance to the decision boundary.

FMN supports perturbation models based on the l0, l1, l2, and infinity norms. The authors report robustness to hyperparameter choices, no requirement for an already adversarial starting point, and convergence in a small number of lightweight steps. These properties target both setup effort and computation.

Extensive experiments show improvements over existing l0, l1, and infinity-norm attacks in perturbation size, convergence speed, and computation time. Performance is comparable to leading l2 attacks. The findings therefore differ by perturbation model, with the strongest reported advantages outside the l2 case.
neurips-2021-fast-minimum-norm-adversari.tldr: FMN efficiently searches for small adversarial perturbations by adapting its norm constraint across several perturbation models.

paragraphs: Feature attribution seeks to explain a neural network's prediction by identifying important parts of its input. This paper uses predictive information as a proxy for importance, focusing on which input features carry information associated with the network's prediction.

Previous use of this idea identified informative latent features by placing an information bottleneck inside the network. Those features belong to an internal representation, leaving a gap between what is identified within the model and the original input a person wants to understand.

The proposed method places a bottleneck on the input itself. It allows through input features associated with predictive latent features, connecting internal predictive information to fine-grained locations in the input domain. The method is designed to work independently of the network architecture.

The authors compare their approach with several feature-attribution methods using established evaluation experiments. The abstract does not state a comparative ranking. Its central contribution is the mechanism for tracing predictive information back to input features, making this form of explanation available at the level of the original data.
neurips-2021-fine-grained-neural-network.tldr: An input information bottleneck identifies fine-grained features associated with predictive internal representations across network architectures.

paragraphs: Financial observations are often modeled with heavy-tailed distributions, which accommodate extreme values more readily than Gaussian models. Learning a graph of relationships under such distributions introduces mathematical difficulties, including nonconvex optimization, that complicate practical algorithm design.

This paper develops graph estimators within the Markov random field framework under a Student-t data-generating assumption. The distributional choice puts the heavy-tailed nature of the observations directly into the estimation problem, rather than starting from a Gaussian formulation.

The authors design scalable numerical methods using the alternating direction method of multipliers. Their algorithms can learn a connected graph or a graph with k connected components. They also establish theoretical convergence guarantees for the proposed numerical procedures.

Experiments use publicly available observations from the S&P500, foreign exchange markets, and cryptocurrencies. The methods outperform leading benchmarks in the reported evaluations. The contribution combines an explicit heavy-tailed statistical assumption with algorithms for different graph connectivity requirements, supported by both convergence analysis and practical financial-data experiments.
neurips-2021-graphical-models-in-heavy-t.tldr: Student-t graphical models and scalable optimization algorithms improve graph estimation in the reported heavy-tailed financial-data experiments.

paragraphs: The Hessian describes an objective's local curvature, and its eigenvalues reveal how that curvature varies across directions. These quantities support optimization and model analysis, but studying them for nonlinear models often requires strong simplifications.

The paper uses random matrix theory to characterize Hessian eigenvalue distributions for a broad family of nonlinear models extending classical generalized linear models. Its aim is to retain meaningful nonlinear structure while avoiding strong simplifying assumptions used in earlier analyses.

The resulting spectra can differ qualitatively depending on the data, response model, and loss function. Eigenvalues may occupy bounded or unbounded ranges, form one main cluster or several, and include isolated values to either side of the main cluster.

These distinctions show that the shape of a Hessian spectrum depends on several parts of the learning problem, rather than following one uniform pattern. By analyzing a relatively simple but nontrivial model family precisely, the work helps explain possible theoretical origins of striking spectral features observed in more realistic machine-learning models.
neurips-2021-hessian-eigenspectra-of-mor.tldr: Random matrix analysis shows how data, nonlinear responses, and loss functions produce qualitatively different Hessian spectra.

paragraphs: Bayesian deep learning offers benefits such as predictive uncertainty estimates and model selection, but exact neural-network posterior distributions are intractable. The Laplace approximation is a comparatively simple way to approximate those distributions, yet it has been less popular than several alternatives.

The paper examines concerns that the approximation requires expensive Hessian calculations, is hard to implement, or performs poorly. It reviews different variants, including versions with little computational overhead, showing that the practical cost depends on the chosen form.

To make those options accessible, the authors introduce the laplace library for PyTorch. The software provides user-friendly access to the major variants, addressing implementation difficulty alongside the paper's discussion of their computational requirements.

Extensive experiments show performance competitive with more popular alternatives and favorable computational cost. The result supports reconsidering Laplace methods as practical tools for Bayesian deep learning. The contribution combines a review, an implementation resource, and empirical evidence, with the broader aim of making uncertainty-aware modeling easier to adopt.
neurips-2021-laplace-redux-effortless-ba.tldr: A review, PyTorch library, and experiments establish Laplace approximations as practical, computationally efficient alternatives for Bayesian deep learning.

paragraphs: Changing a causal system to reach a desired state is relevant to control, biology, and materials science. This paper studies a specific version of that task: actively choosing shift interventions so that the system reaches a target mean.

The authors first define which causal models remain indistinguishable given information from shift interventions. They then propose two active learning strategies guaranteed to match the desired mean exactly. The strategies focus experimental effort on achieving that target.

A worst-case lower bound establishes a limit on how few interventions can suffice. The proposed strategies attain optimality for certain graph classes. They may also require exponentially fewer interventions than approaches whose objective is to learn the underlying causal graph's structure.

Experiments support the theoretical direction by showing fewer required interventions than several baselines. The key distinction is between learning enough about a system to achieve a particular mean and pursuing structural identification as the main objective. The exponential savings are a possibility established by the analysis, rather than a claim about every causal graph.
neurips-2021-matching-a-desired-causal-s.tldr: Target-focused active learning can identify shift interventions that exactly match a desired mean with far fewer experiments in some causal settings.

paragraphs: When positive events are rare, retaining every negative example can be expensive. The paper proves that information about unknown parameters is tied to the relatively small positive count, supporting negative sampling. However, reducing negatives to the same number as positives loses information.

The authors study nonuniform sampling, where different negatives have different inclusion probabilities. They derive the asymptotic distribution of an inverse probability weighted estimator and identify sampling probabilities that minimize its variance. This gives a principled way to choose which negatives to retain.

They then develop a likelihood estimator that corrects the sampled data's log odds. It has the smallest asymptotic variance within a large class of estimators and is more robust to misspecification of the pilot estimate. The optimality statement concerns that class and the asymptotic setting.

Validation includes simulations and a click-through dataset containing more than 0.3 trillion observations collected over a month. The theoretical and empirical results support careful sampling and correction as a way to improve estimation efficiency while retaining more of the information relevant to rare events.
neurips-2021-nonuniform-negative-samplin.tldr: Optimized negative sampling and log-odds correction improve parameter estimation efficiency for rare-event data.

paragraphs: The paper considers a fixed family of unknown sparse vectors, each with at most k nonzero entries. A query returns the sign of its inner product with a randomly chosen member of the family, so responses mix information from different unknown vectors.

The first task is support recovery: identifying which coordinates are nonzero in every vector, using noisy responses. The authors prove the existence of learning algorithms without additional assumptions on the vectors beyond the stated problem setup. This addresses structural identification despite both mixing and noise.

The second task seeks approximate recovery of the vectors themselves from error-free responses. For this stronger objective, the authors establish algorithms under a mild structural assumption on the unknown vectors. They also rigorously analyze the number of queries required.

These tasks extend support and approximate recovery from one-bit compressed sensing to mixtures of responses. The results distinguish what can be learned about nonzero locations under noise from what can be reconstructed numerically with noiseless feedback and an extra structural condition.
neurips-2021-on-learning-sparse-vectors-.tldr: The paper establishes algorithms for sparse-vector support recovery from noisy mixed sign responses and conditional approximate recovery from noiseless responses.

paragraphs: Variational methods are widely used to analyze network data because they offer tractable approximations to difficult estimation problems. This paper studies their statistical quality for stochastic block models when some network links are missing, a setting relevant to incomplete observations.

Earlier guarantees typically described asymptotic normality when estimating global model parameters. The authors instead establish that a variational approximation to the maximum likelihood estimator converges at the minimax rate in the missing-link setting.

A minimax rate describes the best achievable scaling of estimation error over the model class under study. Matching that rate means the approximation attains the optimal statistical order while remaining computationally tractable. The paper presents this as the first estimator combining those properties for this parameter-estimation problem.

Numerical studies on simulated and real networks complement the theoretical result and confirm advantages over existing methods. The contribution is therefore both computational and statistical: a practical approximate inference procedure receives a strong rate guarantee for network parameter estimation with missing links.
neurips-2021-optimality-of-variational-i.tldr: Variational estimation achieves the minimax convergence rate for stochastic block models with missing links while remaining tractable.

paragraphs: Policy learning often depends on reliable rewards or high-quality expert demonstrations, both of which can be costly or unavailable. This paper develops a unified approach for learning from cheaper, imperfect supervision across reinforcement learning and behavioral cloning.

The method interprets weak supervision as information supplied by a peer agent. It evaluates the learner through correlated agreement with the peer's policy, rather than simple agreement. This changes the objective used to decide whether following the peer is useful.

The approach explicitly penalizes policies that overfit the weak supervision. That matters because imperfect guidance can contain noise as well as helpful information. The framework aims to use the available signal while discouraging a policy from fitting its imperfections too closely.

Alongside theoretical guarantees, the paper reports extensive evaluations with noisy rewards, weak demonstrations, and combined reinforcement-learning and behavioral-cloning training. Performance improves substantially in those experiments, especially as environmental complexity or noise increases. The findings support correlated agreement as a common learning principle across several forms of weak policy supervision.
neurips-2021-policy-learning-using-weak-.tldr: Evaluating correlated agreement with an imperfect peer enables policy learning from weak supervision while penalizing overfitting to that guidance.

paragraphs: Learned optimizers are algorithms whose update rules are themselves trained. Their flexible nonlinear parameterizations can improve performance, but also make it hard to understand how they work or why they might outperform carefully tuned conventional optimizers.

The paper analyzes and visualizes learned optimizers trained from scratch on four distinct tasks. It asks whether their behavior can be understood as combinations of familiar optimization techniques or whether they have developed different mechanisms.

The authors identify recognizable behaviors including momentum, gradient clipping, and learning-rate schedules. They also find new forms of learning-rate adaptation. Beyond naming these behaviors, the analysis examines how internal dynamics and mechanisms coordinate the computations that produce them.

The findings show that the studied learned optimizers admit meaningful mechanistic interpretations despite their complex parameterizations. They reveal both rediscovery of established techniques and additional adaptive behavior. The work also develops tools for interpreting future learned optimizers, making their internal operation a subject of analysis alongside their observed optimization performance.
neurips-2021-reverse-engineering-learned.tldr: Analysis of learned optimizers reveals familiar optimization techniques alongside new learning-rate adaptations and the internal mechanisms coordinating them.

paragraphs: Some structured datasets contain repeated event observations rather than a single number for each entry. This paper studies a matrix whose entries are marked point processes and seeks to cluster its rows, identifying heterogeneity across the repeatedly observed data.

The proposed mixture model uses multiple levels of marked point processes. More specifically, each matrix entry is modeled as a marked log-Gaussian Cox process. This supplies a statistical framework in which the repeated event patterns can inform the grouping of rows.

For estimation, the authors combine a semiparametric Expectation-Solution algorithm with functional principal component analysis of point processes. The combination is presented as an efficient way to fit the model while working with the functional structure of the event data.

Simulation studies and analyses of real data demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The central contribution is bringing row clustering to a matrix whose entries have their own stochastic event structure, with a model and estimation procedure designed for that richer form of observation.
neurips-2021-row-clustering-of-a-point-p.tldr: A multilevel mixture model clusters rows of event-process matrices using an efficient estimation procedure built around functional principal components.

paragraphs: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics combines gradient-based updates with randomness. This paper studies its generalization error in nonconvex problems when the learning rate stays constant, assuming smoothness and dissipativity. Those conditions define the setting in which the guarantees hold.

The main result is a bound that does not depend on the amount of training time and approaches zero as the sample size grows. Compared with time-dependent bounds, it gives control that does not become weaker simply because the algorithm runs longer.

The proof uses uniform stability, which examines how changing a training sample affects the learning procedure. The authors exploit a Wasserstein contraction property of the corresponding Langevin diffusion to control that sensitivity. This also avoids needing gradient bounds imposed through Lipschitz-like assumptions.

The analysis extends to variants using different discretizations, Euclidean projections, and non-isotropic noise. Its significance is a generalization guarantee that remains useful over time while accommodating several algorithmic forms, within the stated smoothness and dissipativity setting.
neurips-2021-time-independent-generaliza.tldr: Under smoothness and dissipativity, constant-rate SGLD admits generalization bounds that are independent of training time and vanish with growing sample size.

paragraphs: A classifier can predict accurately while expressing too much confidence. This paper examines that calibration problem for heavily overparameterized models trained with little data, focusing on the interaction among data augmentation, model ensembles, and calibration after training.

The authors show that combining models does not necessarily improve calibration. Standard ensembling can even worsen it when paired with techniques such as mixup regularization. Consequently, the accuracy gains from an ensemble do not by themselves establish that its confidence estimates are more reliable.

The paper finds that calibration methods such as temperature scaling need adjustment for ensembles and should be applied after the predictions have been averaged. The order matters because the confidence estimates ultimately used are those of the combined predictor.

In low-data simulations across several classification benchmarks, this strategy can halve Expected Calibration Error relative to standard deep ensembles. The result supports treating calibration of the final ensemble as its own step, while preserving the distinction between empirical calibration improvements and the accuracy benefits of ensembling.
neurips-2021-uncertainty-quantification-.tldr: Deep ensembles can worsen calibration, but calibrating after averaging can substantially improve confidence estimates in low-data settings.

paragraphs: Speech-enhancement systems estimate clean speech from noisy recordings. Their training and deployment conditions can differ, creating a domain shift that complicates learning. This paper addresses adaptation to a target domain using knowledge available from a source domain.

The proposed discriminator-constrained optimal transport network, DOTN, performs that adaptation without target-domain supervision. It aims to estimate clean references for noisy target speech, treating enhancement as a regression task with continuous outputs.

DOTN combines optimal transport with a generative adversarial framework. The discriminator constraint extends the classical transport formulation to help evaluate continuous target-domain labels. This addresses a setting where unsupervised adaptation methods are less developed than in classification and often require additional input information.

Experiments on two speech-enhancement tasks show improvements over previous adversarial domain-adaptation frameworks in a purely unsupervised setting. The contribution is a transport-based adaptation mechanism tailored to continuous speech outputs, with the reported results supporting its usefulness when noise conditions differ between the source and target domains.
neurips-2021-unsupervised-noise-adaptive.tldr: DOTN combines optimal transport and adversarial learning to adapt speech enhancement to new noise domains without target supervision.

paragraphs: Epidemic forecasts are useful for public-health planning only if their uncertainty is also meaningful. The paper addresses forecasting systems that neglect uncertainty, as well as practical difficulties with alternatives such as specifying Bayesian neural-network priors or running computationally expensive ensembles.

EpiFNP uses a neural functional process to represent a probability distribution over future epidemic values in a nonparametric way. This makes uncertainty part of the forecasting model itself, through a probabilistic generative account of the time series.

A dynamic stochastic correlation graph represents relationships among sequences. Different stochastic latent variables capture functional uncertainty from multiple perspectives. By learning connections between the current season and similar historical patterns, the model also gives an interpretable basis for its forecasts.

In real-time flu forecasting experiments, EpiFNP significantly outperforms leading models in accuracy and calibration, with reported improvements up to 2.5 times and 2.4 times, respectively. These results support both prediction quality and uncertainty quality in that setting. The authors also suggest potential relevance to uncertainty estimation in other deep sequential models.
neurips-2021-when-in-doubt-neural-non-pa.tldr: EpiFNP models epidemic forecasts and their uncertainty jointly, improving accuracy and calibration in real-time flu forecasting experiments.

paragraphs: Standard self-attention lets every image token interact with every other token, providing flexible global modeling. Its time and memory costs grow quadratically with the number of tokens, making long sequences and high-resolution images expensive to process.

The paper changes the direction of attention. Cross-covariance attention operates between feature channels rather than between tokens, using a cross-covariance matrix derived from keys and queries to determine the interactions. Its complexity grows linearly with the number of tokens.

The resulting XCiT architecture is built around this operation. It aims to retain conventional transformers' accuracy while achieving scalability associated with convolutional architectures. The change directly targets the token-count bottleneck that becomes more severe as image resolution increases.

The authors report strong results for ImageNet-1k classification and self-supervised feature learning, COCO object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20k semantic segmentation. These evaluations support the architecture's usefulness across several visual tasks, while the linear token complexity explains its appeal for efficiently handling higher-resolution inputs.
neurips-2021-xcit-cross-covariance-image.tldr: XCiT moves attention from token pairs to feature channels, achieving linear token complexity and strong results across several vision tasks.
